lessons.title: The certificate profile
lessons.why: SIP never starts if TLS fails. Dial-plan debates can wait.
body: Issue a certificate whose subject or SAN contains the SBC FQDN, from a CA in the Microsoft trusted root program, with server authentication EKU. Generate the CSR on the SBC. A private lab CA is how you learn the failure, not how you run production.
TLS 1.2 or newer toward the proxies. TLS 1.0 is not a compatible offer. Include the chain. An incomplete chain looks like a mysterious timeout.
lessons.say: Public CA, SAN matches the paired FQDN, server EKU, TLS 1.2 or newer.
lessons.fault: The chain is missing and the handshake times out.
lessons.listen: The SBC certificate must match the paired name, come from a trusted public CA, and speak TLS 1.2 or newer.

lessons.title: Names, wildcards, and the paired FQDN
lessons.why: A certificate can be valid and still be the wrong name.
body: The name Teams checks is the FQDN you configured on the gateway. A wildcard is acceptable when it follows RFC 2818. A certificate for www.contoso.com does not cover sbc1.contoso.com.
If you add a sip subdomain, verify that domain in the tenant before you pair it. DNS must resolve publicly. Split-horizon DNS that only works inside the office will not help Microsoft’s proxies.

flow.label: Cert
flow.detail: That name or a legal wildcard

lessons.say: The certificate name, the DNS name, and the paired FQDN are the same name.
lessons.fault: TLS fails with a name mismatch and someone restarts the SBC instead.
lessons.listen: The certificate, public DNS, and the paired FQDN must agree. Wildcards only help when RFC 2818 says they match.

lessons.title: Three SIP proxies and failover
lessons.why: The service tells the SBC which proxy is nearest and fails between them. Your firewall has to allow all of them.
body: Commercial clouds use sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com, sip2, and sip3, on TCP 5061. IPv6 names exist on the plan page. GCC High uses sip.pstnhub.gov.teams.microsoft.us. DoD uses sip.pstnhub.dod.teams.microsoft.us. Those government clouds do not use the commercial trio.

The names resolve into published ranges, including 52.112.0.0/14 and 52.120.0.0/14 for commercial media and signaling as listed on the plan page checked 14 October 2026. Allow the ranges. Re-read the page when you change the firewall. Microsoft moves addresses.

lessons.title: SIP OPTIONS
lessons.why: OPTIONS are how Teams decides the trunk is willing. A dial plan cannot heal a trunk that does not answer.
body: Teams sends SIP OPTIONS to the SBC. The SBC should answer while it is in service. The admin center shows SBC status from that health. This campus does not pretend to know Microsoft’s private failure counter. Repeated misses are a reason to pull the trunk from the route and look at the log.
Answer on the signaling interface, not the management port. Rehearse a failure. A second gateway that has never seen an INVITE is untested.
lessons.say: I treat missed OPTIONS as a trunk problem and I look at the admin-center status beside the SBC log.
lessons.fault: A script fails over on a single lost packet and flaps the trunk all day.
lessons.listen: SIP OPTIONS tell you the SBC is alive. Pull a trunk that keeps missing them, and do not invent a magic counter.

lessons.title: Codecs and SRTP
lessons.why: An empty codec list is a 488. Missing media ports is silence after a 200.
body: Direct Routing lists SILK, G.711, G.722, G.729, and AMR-WB for non-bypass calls. Offer a codec both sides have. G.711 µ-law and A-law both belong if the carrier is vague. Media is SRTP. A trunk that offers only plaintext RTP is not the design.
DTMF has to survive every hop or the IVR never hears 1. Test digits through the carrier, not only Teams-to-Teams. If bypass is on, do not depend on AMR-WB.

chart.title: Safe minimum
chart.note: What to offer unless you measured a reason not to.

lessons.say: I offer G.711, I use SRTP, and I test DTMF through the carrier.
lessons.fault: The SBC allows only a codec Teams will not use on that path, and every call is 488.
lessons.listen: Agree a codec, keep SRTP, and prove DTMF through the SBC. AMR-WB is not a bypass codec.

lessons.title: Failover you can rehearse
lessons.why: The outage should not be the first test of the second proxy or the second SBC.
body: In a window, break the primary path and place a call. You want to see the next proxy or the next gateway take it, and you want emergency calls to prefer the local SBC still. Write the timestamps.
Certificate expiry is a failover you can predict. Put the date on a calendar and renew before Saturday morning becomes the test.
lessons.say: I rehearse failover and I know the certificate expiry date.
lessons.fault: The second SBC has never received a call, and the certificate expires on a Saturday.
lessons.listen: Rehearse the second gateway, and renew the certificate before it expires.
